outcome: Maternal perceptions of health care services
cohort: 6,421 mothers of singletons in Canada (unweighted sample), representing a weighted sample of 76,508 mothers
finding: Significant socioeconomic disparities were found across a range of maternal and child health outcomes in Canada, with stronger gradients observed for maternal and infant health status indicators compared to other health service utilization outcomes.
mod_finding: Negative associations were observed between some socioeconomic position measures and cesarean section rates.
